# find_missing_game_assets

[← Command index](README.md)

Compare the games in the Pegasus metadata with the asset files in the local locker.

## Synopsis

```
find_missing_game_assets [options]
```

## Description

For every entry in every Pegasus metadata file, checks whether each asset type
(Background, BoxBack, BoxFront, Label, Screenshot, Video) exists at its expected path
under the Local locker's `Gaming/Assets` folder. It then reports the missing assets per
type, and the extra files in the assets folder that no metadata entry accounts for.

Each non-empty list is written in full to a file in the current directory:
`Missing_<AssetType>.txt` and `Extras.txt`. The log shows only the totals, or the first
and last few items with `-v`.

## Options

### Common options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-v, --verbose` | Enable verbose mode. |
| `-p, --pretend_run` | Do a pretend run with no permanent changes. |
| `-x, --exit_on_failure` | Enable exit on failure mode. |
| `--no-preview` | Skip the preview confirmation prompt. |

## Examples

### Report missing and extra assets

```bash
find_missing_game_assets
```

### Also show sample items in the log

```bash
find_missing_game_assets -v
```

### Report without writing the list files

```bash
find_missing_game_assets -p -v
```

## Notes

- Run it from a scratch directory; the report files land in whatever directory you run it from and overwrite earlier ones.
